targetText: Fascism is the concentrated expression of the general offensive undertaken by the world bourgeoisie against the proletariat. Its overthrow is therefore an absolute necessity, nay, it is even a question of the every-day existence and of the bread and butter of every ordinary worker.
summary: Fascism is the concentrated offensive of big capital against the working class and its daily survival.
explanation: Zetkin establishes that fascism is not an isolated political aberration, but the generalized offensive of the capitalist ruling class to crush working-class living standards and organizations.

targetText: Fascism, on the contrary, viewed objectively, is not the revenge of the bourgeoisie in retaliation for proletarian aggression against the bourgeoisie, but it is a punishment of the proletariat for failing to carry on the revolution begun in Russia. The Fascist leaders are not a small and exclusive caste; they extend deeply into wide elements of the population.
summary: Unlike a narrow military junta, fascism is a mass movement that punishes the working class for an uncompleted socialist revolution.
explanation: Contrasting Mussolini's movement with Admiral Horthy's officer clique in Hungary, Zetkin explains that fascism builds a broad social base among displaced layers of society when reformist betrayal stalls proletarian revolution.

targetText: Fascism, with all its forcefulness in the prosecution of its violent deeds, is indeed nothing else but the expression of the disintegration and decay of capitalist economy, and the symptom of the dissolution of the bourgeois State.
summary: Fascist violence is not a sign of capitalist vitality, but a symptom of capitalist economic decay and state crisis.
explanation: Where social-democratic reformists cowered before the supposed invulnerability of the bourgeoisie, Zetkin shows that the ruling class turns to fascism precisely because normal parliamentary institutions and capitalist economics are breaking down.

targetText: The second root of Fascism lies in the retarding of the world revolution by the treacherous attitude of the reformist leaders. Large numbers of the petty bourgeoisie, including even the middle classes, had discarded their war-time psychology for a certain sympathy with reformist socialism, hoping that the latter would bring about a reformation of society along democratic lines. They were disappointed in their hopes.
summary: Social-democratic betrayal of socialist revolution drives ruined middle strata and disillusioned workers into the arms of fascism.
explanation: When reformist leaders collaborate with the bourgeoisie instead of overthrowing capitalism, impoverished petty-bourgeois layers and demoralized workers lose faith in socialism and seek refuge in fascist demagogy.

targetText: Fascism has diverse characteristics in different countries. Nevertheless it has two distinguishing features in all countries, namely, the pretence of a revolutionary programme, which is cleverly adapted to the interests and demands of the large masses, and, on the other hand, the application of the most brutal violence.
summary: The dual weapon of fascism everywhere: pseudo-revolutionary anti-capitalist demagogy combined with brutal anti-worker terror.
explanation: Zetkin identifies the universal formula of fascism: it wins mass support by mimicking anti-elitist, revolutionary slogans appealing to ruined lower classes, while deploying paramilitary terror squads against organized labor.

targetText: The Fascist Party created a double-edged weapon for the corruption and terrorisation of the working class. For the corruption of the working class the Fascist Trade Unions were created, the so-called corporations in which workers and employers were united. To terrorise the working class, the Fascist Party created the militant squads which had grown out of the punitive expeditions.
summary: Fascist corporatism corrupts labor through class-collaborationist unions while Blackshirt squads terrorize independent workers.
explanation: In Italy, Mussolini paired Yellow "corporations" (uniting bosses and workers to suppress strikes) with armed paramilitary squads funded by industrialists and landlords to smash revolutionary unions.

targetText: The destruction of the trade unions has enabled the employers to effect wage reductions of 20 to 30 per cent, and in some cases of even 50 to 60 per cent.
summary: Once in power, fascism immediately abandons its social promises and enforces massive wage cuts and privatization for big capital.
explanation: Zetkin documents Mussolini's actual economic record in office: dismantling the eight-hour day, outlawing factory councils, slashing wages by up to 60 percent, abolishing luxury and capital taxes on the rich, and raising indirect taxes on workers.

targetText: The Third International is, in contradistinction to the old International, an International of all races without any distinctions whatever.
summary: Zetkin affirms that the Communist International unites working people of all races without any racial hierarchy or colonial chauvinism.
explanation: Contrasting the Comintern with the European-chauvinist Second International (which tolerated colonialism), Zetkin emphasizes that revolutionary communism is built on uncompromising racial equality and global anti-imperialist solidarity.

targetText: The Communist Parties must not only be the vanguard of the proletarian manual workers, but also the energetic defenders of the interests of the brain workers. They must be the leaders of all sections of society which are driven into opposition to bourgeois domination because of their interests and their expectations of the future.
summary: To defeat fascism ideologically, Communist Parties must lead manual workers, intellectual workers, and small peasants alike.
explanation: Zetkin argues that communists cannot allow fascism to monopolize ruined intellectuals, civil servants, and small peasants; the Party must champion all strata crushed by monopoly capital under the banner of a Workers' and Peasants' Government.

targetText: The proletariat must have a well organised apparatus of self-defence. Whenever Fascism uses violence, it must be met with proletarian violence. I do not mean by this individual terrorist acts, but the violence of the organised revolutionary class struggle of the proletariat. Germany has made a beginning by organising factory "hundreds." This struggle can only be successful if there is a proletarian united front. The workers must unite for this struggle regardless of party.
summary: Defeating fascism requires a Proletarian United Front across party lines and organized armed working-class self-defense.
explanation: Rejecting both passive parliamentary appeals and isolated individual terrorism, Zetkin calls for an all-worker United Front and organized workplace defense squads (factory "hundreds") to crush fascist paramilitaries and overthrow capitalism.
